clue.text: A coin concealed is a pest in the garden

parts.note: P stands for a penny, the small British coin
concealed means hid, kept out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone hides a coin, which apparently counts as a garden nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as pests.

clue.text: They break down, we hear, these keepers of old records

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver to go by how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: people who break things down into parts to study them are analysts

explanation.surface: People who suffer breakdowns turn out to be the custodians of ancient archives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break down' suggests collapsing in tears, but here it means dissecting a problem, as analysts do.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are year-by-year historical chronicles, and their compilers are the people who keep such records.

clue.text: Drunk on home-brew at afternoon repast

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: drunk means high, intoxicated
tea is the drink most often brewed at home

explanation.surface: Someone gets tipsy on homemade beer at a late-afternoon snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home-brew' suggests beer, but the brew made in every British home is tea.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is a substantial early-evening meal with tea, cooked food and bread, served in place of dinner.

clue.text: Wood trade

definitions.meaning: pine or fir timber sawn into planks
to buy and sell, do business

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is fir or pine planking, and to deal is to do business in goods.

clue.text: Chief spirit in port

definitions.meaning: an angel of the highest rank, such as Michael or Gabriel
a Russian port on the White Sea, Arkhangelsk

explanation.definitionFit: The senior angels are given this title, and it is also the English name of a northern Russian seaport.

clue.text: Changes his work to include Bob Major, for example

definitions.text: Changes his work to include Bob Major, for example

parts.words: Changes his work to include Bob Major, for example
parts.note: read as a person whose job involves change-ringing, where Bob Major is one of the set methods for eight bells

explanation.surface: A man alters his job description to take in a senior officer named Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: In bell-ringing, 'changes' are the orders in which bells sound, and Bob Major is a ringing method on eight bells, not an army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer, or student of the art of ringing, works through changes and methods such as Bob Major.

clue.text: How much land is needed for a medley-race?

indicators.note: a medley is a jumble or mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A question about how big a field you need to stage a mixed swimming relay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley-race' looks like the swimming event; split it, and 'medley' mixes up the four letters of 'race'. 'is needed for a' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of land measure equal to 4,840 square yards, so it answers the question of a plot's size.

clue.text: Light fitter more idle after midnight

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other one

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
more idle means lazier

explanation.surface: An electrician installing lamps is even lazier once it is past midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' means a window pane here, not a lamp; 'midnight' is the middle of the word night, which is G.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier fits panes of glass, and a window pane is called a light.

clue.text: Left port carrying cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship sailed out of harbour loaded with goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel loaded with freight is said to be heavily burdened.

clue.text: Curmudgeon pulling back endlessly

indicators.note: back means the trimmed word is read in the opposite direction
endlessly means the last letter of the word for pulling is cut off

parts.note: pulling means dragging

explanation.surface: A grumpy old man is hauling something backwards without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final G of DRAGGING to give DRAGGIN, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a miser, the kind of mean, cantankerous person also called a curmudgeon.

clue.text: Remove poisons from meat contained in stew

indicators.note: a stew is a jumbled mixture, so the letters of these words are thrown together

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to clean toxins out of the meat in a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' sounds like the dish the meat is in, but 'in stew' is the anagram signal; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decontaminate is to cleanse something of harmful substances such as toxins or radiation.

clue.text: A dimmer-switch for the theatre

indicators.note: to switch is to change round, so these letters swap places

explanation.surface: A lighting control designed for use on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dimmer-switch' reads as stage lighting, but 'switch' rearranges A DIMMER. The Mermaid is a London theatre; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mermaid Theatre is a well-known playhouse at Blackfriars in the City of London.

clue.text: Reluctant crowd going to hospital

parts.note: a crowd or group of people can be called a lot

explanation.surface: A gathering of people heads to A&E without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth, also spelt loath, means unwilling or disinclined.

clue.text: Bit of a fight

explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a tiny piece of something, and informally a scrap is also a brief fistfight.

clue.text: Northern friend of Tom Sawyer

definitions.meaning: an adjective standing for a native of Finland, a northern European
Huckleberry, Tom Sawyer's companion in Mark Twain's novels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' reads as describing the friend, but it is a separate definition: a northern European from Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland is a northern European, and Huckleberry is Tom Sawyer's friend in Mark Twain's stories.

clue.text: Mature advertisement last month

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, is old commercial letter-writing shorthand for last month

explanation.surface: An advert that ran a month ago was a grown-up one.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) was used in old business letters: 'your letter of the 5th ult.' meant the 5th of last month.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is fully grown, so mature in years.

clue.text: Euclid's fifth proposition perfect in conception

indicators.note: fifth asks for the letter in fifth position of the Greek mathematician's name

parts.note: a proposition is an offer, a deal

explanation.surface: The fifth theorem in Euclid's geometry is judged flawless in its design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Euclid's fifth proposition' sounds like a geometry theorem; in fact the fifth letter of EUCLID, I, is followed by DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, especially as it exists only as an idea in the mind.

clue.text: Instruction to banker footing organisation

parts.note: a footing or position is a standing
organisation, as in arrangement, is order

explanation.surface: A banker is told to put the firm's affairs on a sound basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footing' looks like a verb about paying the bill, but it is a noun meaning status.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer's standing instruction to a bank to pay a fixed sum regularly to someone.

clue.text: Lady of the house?

parts.note: house here means a family line, as in a royal house, so the lady is a female relative

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests the woman in charge of a home; 'house' in the sense of a family line gives a female relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinswoman is a female relative, a woman belonging to the same family or dynasty.

clue.text: All robotic on a roundabout, like Gilbert and Sullivan's work

indicators.note: roundabout signals that the letters go round and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Robots ride a fairground carousel in the manner of a Savoy opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like a traffic junction or fairground ride, but it signals the letters going round into a new order; 'like' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert wrote the words and Sullivan the music, so their operas were a joint effort by two partners.

clue.text: Fielder liable to infection

definitions.meaning: the baseball fielder behind home plate, or any fielder who takes the ball
an adjective phrase standing for someone who picks up illnesses easily

explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a fielder crouches behind the batter to take the pitch, and a person who picks up every bug is jokingly one who catches things.

clue.text: Tooth found in Channel Islands, first set with gold

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off the French coast

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word set

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A tooth turns up in Jersey or Guernsey, its front one capped in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link; 'with gold' adds OR, the heraldic term for gold, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the sharp cutting teeth at the front of the mouth.

clue.text: Prepares places

definitions.meaning: gets ready, as one readies a table or a trap

explanation.definitionFit: To set a table is to prepare it, and to set something down is to place it.

clue.text: Tree French author raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the name is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer, author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A French writer grew up among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree with red autumn leaves, its berries used as a spice.

clue.text: End of motorway illuminated all round

indicators.note: all round means one word surrounds the other

parts.note: illuminated means lit
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written here as M and I

explanation.surface: The final stretch of a motorway is lit up on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary, the point beyond which something cannot go.

clue.text: Barge company in Devon area

indicators.note: in means this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Devon lies in the South West of England, abbreviated SW

explanation.surface: A firm operating barges somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in the South West of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used to carry cargo, a kind of lighter.

clue.text: Cram to get through forty-five degrees?

indicators.note: get through means this word passes inside the other

parts.note: south-west lies forty-five degrees between south and west, so SW

explanation.surface: Someone tries to pack things in while turning through an eighth of a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'forty-five degrees' stands for a compass point midway between two others, here SW.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or squeeze things away tightly, just as to cram is.

clue.text: The French step over southern canyon

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: pas is the French word for a step, as in ballet

explanation.surface: A French dance step performed above a gorge in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' wants to be LE or LA; here the whole phrase gives the French word PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a narrow route through mountains, like a gorge or ravine.

clue.text: Adept with sage in India?

definitions.meaning: in Theosophy, a master who has attained great spiritual knowledge
a wise man revered in the subcontinent, as Gandhi was

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophists call an enlightened master by this title, and in India it honours a great soul, famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Time to buy the freedom of a cross member in the house

definitions.text: a cross member in the house

parts.note: to ransom a captive is to pay for their release

explanation.surface: It is time to pay to free an MP who has switched sides in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross member in the house' suggests an angry MP; it is a horizontal beam in a building. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal bar across a window or above a door, a crosspiece in a building's frame.

clue.text: Acrobatic turn that might impress the field

definitions.meaning: a sideways handspring with arms and legs spread
the wheel of a farm wagon could leave an impression in a field's soil

explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast's sideways handspring, and literally the wheel of a farm vehicle that ruts the ground.

clue.text: Male parent to name a sea-nymph

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A father names his daughter after a mythical sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens were sea creatures who lured sailors with song.
